I used to have Sprint, and with sprint, my service was integrated with google voice. During that time, i got close to zero robocalls. Pure bliss. Once I left sprint, (and the integration with GV ended) the robocalls went through the roof. I run an app that is supposed to block them, but the phone still rings once or twice before getting hung up. Kind of irritating.

These guys are using fake phone numbers as well, so after I block one number they call from another. Hard to fight that kind enemy. This is one case where my libertarian ideals are being tested. Perhaps phone numbers could be considered private property, and thus if they are called without permission it could be seen as criminal trespass.

I saw on the news recently about this same topic, several congresspersons were saying that the phone companies (Verizon, sprint, etc) have a capability to stop these calls. It's also mentioned in this article. I think we will soon see the FCC intend to stop these calls. I just wonder how long it will take the telecoms to act.
